# wyhash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wyhash/

## Expand description

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
(faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
no dependencies.

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt) although the speed varies
([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different the results.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-see-also-examples-folder)Usage (see also examples folder)

For the hashing function you can use either the free function or the
`Hasher` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#wyhash-function-usage)`wyhash` function usage

```
use wyhash::wyhash;
let data = [0, 1, 2];
let seed = 3;
let hash = wyhash(&data, seed);
println!("{:x}", hash); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hasher-trait-usage)`Hasher` trait usage

You can also use `std::hash::Hasher`, it is the same.

```
use core::hash::Hasher;
use wyhash::WyHash;
let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
println!("{:x}", hasher.finish()); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#wyrng-function-usage)`wyrng` function usage

Note that the seed parameter is updated so that it is possible to generate a sequence of random numbers.

```
use wyhash::wyrng;
let mut seed = 3;
let random_number = wyrng(&mut seed);
println!("{:x}", random_number); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
println!("{:x}", seed); //prints a0761d6478bd6432
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rngcore-trait-usage)`RngCore` trait usage

You can also use `rand::Rng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::RngCore;
use wyhash::WyRng;
let mut rng = WyRng::default();
println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
```
[§](https://docs.rs#seedablerng-trait-usage)`SeedableRng` trait usage

You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};
use wyhash::WyRng;
// Seeds are 8-byte long.
let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
// Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyhash](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyhash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyrng](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyrng.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHash](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHasherBuilder](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHasherBuilder.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyRng](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyRng.html);

# wyhash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wyhash/0.6.0/wyhash/

## Expand description

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
(faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
no dependencies.

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt) although the speed varies
([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better

Beware that this feature produces different the results.

# wyhash 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/latest

# wyhash fast portable non-cryptographic hashing algorithm

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark (faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need hardware support, can be
used in `no_std` environments) and has no dependencies (except the traits from `rand_core`).

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated [here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt)
although the speed varies ([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

## Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different results.

## Usage

This crate provides free functions as well as implementations of the `Hasher`, `BuildHasher`, `Rng` and
`SeedableRng` traits.

```
use Hasher;
use WyHash;
```
See further examples of the hasher and RNG in the documentation.

## Performance comparison

A basic performance comparison benchmark against [ fnv](https://crates.io/crates/fnv),

[,](https://crates.io/crates/twox-hash)

`twox-hash`[and the standard hash_map hash](https://crates.io/crates/metrohash)

`metrohash`[is included in the sources and you can run it with nightly Rust:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/hash_map/struct.DefaultHasher.html)

`collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher````
cargo +nightly bench
```
## Support

For questions, issues, feature requests, and other changes, please file an
[issue in the github project](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues).

## Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.63.0 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

at your option.

# rand_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rand_core/^0.9/

## Expand description

Random number generation traits

This crate is mainly of interest to crates publishing implementations of
[ RngCore](https://docs.rs/trait.RngCore.html). Other users are encouraged to use the

[crate instead which re-exports the main traits and error types.](https://docs.rs/rand)

`rand`[ RngCore](https://docs.rs/trait.RngCore.html) is the core trait implemented by algorithmic pseudo-random number
generators and external random-number sources.

[ SeedableRng](https://docs.rs/trait.SeedableRng.html) is an extension trait for construction from fixed seeds and
other random number generators.

The [ impls](https://docs.rs/impls/index.html) and

[sub-modules include a few small functions to assist implementation of](https://docs.rs/le/index.html)

`le`[.](https://docs.rs/trait.RngCore.html)

`RngCore`## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [block](https://docs.rs/block/index.html)
- The `BlockRngCore`trait and implementation helpers
- [impls](https://docs.rs/impls/index.html)
- Helper functions for implementing `RngCore`functions.
- [le](https://docs.rs/le/index.html)
- Little-Endian utilities

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [OsError](https://docs.rs/struct.OsError.html)- `os_rng`
- Error type of `OsRng`
- [OsRng](https://docs.rs/struct.OsRng.html)- `os_rng`
- An interface over the operating-system’s random data source
- [RngRead](https://docs.rs/struct.RngReadAdapter.html)- Adapter - `std`
- Adapter that enables reading through a `io::Read``RngCore`
- [Unwrap](https://docs.rs/struct.UnwrapErr.html)- Err
- Wrapper around `TryRngCore``RngCore`
- [Unwrap](https://docs.rs/struct.UnwrapMut.html)- Mut
- Wrapper around `TryRngCore``RngCore`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Crypto](https://docs.rs/trait.CryptoRng.html)- Rng
- A marker trait over `RngCore`
- [RngCore](https://docs.rs/trait.RngCore.html)
- Implementation-level interface for RNGs
- [Seedable](https://docs.rs/trait.SeedableRng.html)- Rng
- A random number generator that can be explicitly seeded.

- A marker trait over `TryRngCore`
- [TryRng](https://docs.rs/trait.TryRngCore.html)- Core
- A potentially fallible variant of `RngCore`

# fnv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fnv/^1/

## Expand description

An implementation of the [Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function](http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#about)About

The FNV hash function is a custom `Hasher` implementation that is more
efficient for smaller hash keys.

[The Rust FAQ states that](https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US/faq.html#why-are-rusts-hashmaps-slow) while the default `Hasher` implementation,
SipHash, is good in many cases, it is notably slower than other algorithms
with short keys, such as when you have a map of integers to other values.
In cases like these, [FNV is demonstrably faster](https://cglab.ca/~abeinges/blah/hash-rs/).

Its disadvantages are that it performs badly on larger inputs, and provides no protection against collision attacks, where a malicious user can craft specific keys designed to slow a hasher down. Thus, it is important to profile your program to ensure that you are using small hash keys, and be certain that your program could not be exposed to malicious inputs (including being a networked server).

The Rust compiler itself uses FNV, as it is not worried about denial-of-service attacks, and can assume that its inputs are going to be small—a perfect use case for FNV.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-fnv-in-a-hashmap)Using FNV in a `HashMap`

The `FnvHashMap` type alias is the easiest way to use the standard library’s
`HashMap` with FNV.

```
use fnv::FnvHashMap;
let mut map = FnvHashMap::default();
map.insert(1, "one");
map.insert(2, "two");
map = FnvHashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(10, Default::default());
map.insert(1, "one");
map.insert(2, "two");
```
Note, the standard library’s `HashMap::new` and `HashMap::with_capacity`
are only implemented for the `RandomState` hasher, so using `Default` to
get the hasher is the next best option.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-fnv-in-a-hashset)Using FNV in a `HashSet`

Similarly, `FnvHashSet` is a type alias for the standard library’s `HashSet`
with FNV.

```
use fnv::FnvHashSet;
let mut set = FnvHashSet::default();
set.insert(1);
set.insert(2);
set = FnvHashSet::with_capacity_and_hasher(10, Default::default());
set.insert(1);
set.insert(2);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [FnvHasher](https://docs.rs/struct.FnvHasher.html)
- An implementation of the Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [FnvBuild](https://docs.rs/type.FnvBuildHasher.html)- Hasher
- A builder for default FNV hashers.
- [FnvHash](https://docs.rs/type.FnvHashMap.html)- Map
- A `HashMap`using a default FNV hasher.
- [FnvHash](https://docs.rs/type.FnvHashSet.html)- Set
- A `HashSet`using a default FNV hasher.

# metrohash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/metrohash/^1/

## Expand description

A Rust implementation of the MetroHash algorithm.

MetroHash is a high quality, high performance hash algorithm

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use metrohash::MetroHashMap;
let mut hash = MetroHashMap::default();
hash.insert(1000, "1000");
assert_eq!(hash.get(&1000), Some(&"1000"));
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Metro](https://docs.rs/type.MetroBuildHasher.html)- Build - Hasher
- A builder for MetroHash.
- [Metro](https://docs.rs/type.MetroHash.html)- Hash
- [Metro](https://docs.rs/type.MetroHashMap.html)- Hash - Map
- A `HashMap`using a default MetroHash.
- [Metro](https://docs.rs/type.MetroHashSet.html)- Hash - Set
- A `HashSet`using a default MetroHash.

# twox_hash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/twox-hash/^2.1/

## Expand description

A Rust implementation of the [xxHash](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash) algorithm.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

These examples use [ XxHash64](https://docs.rs/xxhash64/struct.Hasher.html) but the same ideas can be
used for

[,](https://docs.rs/xxhash32/struct.Hasher.html)

`XxHash32`[, or](https://docs.rs/xxhash3_64/struct.Hasher.html)

`XxHash3_64`[.](https://docs.rs/xxhash3_128/struct.Hasher.html)

`XxHash3_128`[§](https://docs.rs#hashing-arbitrary-data)Hashing arbitrary data

[§](https://docs.rs#when-all-the-data-is-available-at-once)When all the data is available at once

```
use twox_hash::XxHash64;
let seed = 1234;
let hash = XxHash64::oneshot(seed, b"some bytes");
assert_eq!(0xeab5_5659_a496_d78b, hash);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#when-the-data-is-streaming)When the data is streaming

```
use std::hash::Hasher as _;
use twox_hash::XxHash64;
let seed = 1234;
let mut hasher = XxHash64::with_seed(seed);
hasher.write(b"some");
hasher.write(b" ");
hasher.write(b"bytes");
let hash = hasher.finish();
assert_eq!(0xeab5_5659_a496_d78b, hash);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#with-a-default-seed)With a default seed

```
use std::{collections::HashMap, hash::BuildHasherDefault};
use twox_hash::XxHash64;
let mut hash = HashMap::<_, _, BuildHasherDefault<XxHash64>>::default();
hash.insert(42, "the answer");
assert_eq!(hash.get(&42), Some(&"the answer"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#with-a-random-seed)With a random seed

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use twox_hash::xxhash64;
let mut hash = HashMap::<_, _, xxhash64::RandomState>::default();
hash.insert(42, "the answer");
assert_eq!(hash.get(&42), Some(&"the answer"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#with-a-fixed-seed)With a fixed seed

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use twox_hash::xxhash64;
let mut hash = HashMap::with_hasher(xxhash64::State::with_seed(0xdead_cafe));
hash.insert(42, "the answer");
assert_eq!(hash.get(&42), Some(&"the answer"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

| name | description |
|---|---|
| xxhash32 | Include the algorithm`XxHash32` |
| xxhash64 | Include the algorithm`XxHash64` |
| xxhash3_64 | Include the algorithm`XxHash3_64` |
| xxhash3_128 | Include the algorithm`XxHash3_128` |
| random | Create random instances of the hashers |
| serialize | Serialize and deserialize hasher state with Serde |
| std | Use the Rust standard library. Enable this if you want SIMD support in or`XxHash3_64``XxHash3_128` |
| alloc | Use the Rust allocator library. Enable this if you want to create or`XxHash3_64`with dynamic secrets`XxHash3_128` |

[§](https://docs.rs#benchmarks)Benchmarks

See benchmarks in the [comparison](https://github.com/shepmaster/twox-hash/tree/main/comparison) README.

[§](https://docs.rs#contributing)Contributing

- Fork it ([https://github.com/shepmaster/twox-hash/fork](https://github.com/shepmaster/twox-hash/fork))
- Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b my-new-feature`)
- Add a failing test.
- Add code to pass the test.
- Commit your changes (`git commit -am 'Add some feature'`)
- Ensure tests pass.
- Push to the branch (`git push origin my-new-feature`)
- Create a new Pull Request

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use xxhash32::`- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/xxhash32/struct.Hasher.html)as XxHash32;- `xxhash32`
- `pub use xxhash64::`- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/xxhash64/struct.Hasher.html)as XxHash64;- `xxhash64`
- `pub use xxhash3_64::`- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/xxhash3_64/struct.Hasher.html)as XxHash3_64;- `xxhash3_64`
- `pub use xxhash3_128::`- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/xxhash3_128/struct.Hasher.html)as XxHash3_128;- `xxhash3_128`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [xxhash3_](https://docs.rs/xxhash3_64/index.html)- 64 - `xxhash3_64`
- The implementation of XXH3_64.
- [xxhash3_](https://docs.rs/xxhash3_128/index.html)- 128 - `xxhash3_128`
- The implementation of XXH3_128.
- [xxhash32](https://docs.rs/xxhash32/index.html)- `xxhash32`
- The implementation of XXH32.
- [xxhash64](https://docs.rs/xxhash64/index.html)- `xxhash64`
- The implementation of XXH64.

# wyhash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/latest/target-redirect/wyhash/

## Expand description

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
(faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
no dependencies.

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt) although the speed varies
([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different the results.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-see-also-examples-folder)Usage (see also examples folder)

For the hashing function you can use either the free function or the
`Hasher` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#wyhash-function-usage)`wyhash` function usage

```
use wyhash::wyhash;
let data = [0, 1, 2];
let seed = 3;
let hash = wyhash(&data, seed);
println!("{:x}", hash); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hasher-trait-usage)`Hasher` trait usage

You can also use `std::hash::Hasher`, it is the same.

```
use core::hash::Hasher;
use wyhash::WyHash;
let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
println!("{:x}", hasher.finish()); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#wyrng-function-usage)`wyrng` function usage

Note that the seed parameter is updated so that it is possible to generate a sequence of random numbers.

```
use wyhash::wyrng;

let random_number = wyrng(&mut seed);
println!("{:x}", random_number); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
println!("{:x}", seed); //prints a0761d6478bd6432
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rngcore-trait-usage)`RngCore` trait usage

You can also use `rand::Rng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::RngCore;
use wyhash::WyRng;

println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
```
[§](https://docs.rs#seedablerng-trait-usage)`SeedableRng` trait usage

You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};

// Seeds are 8-byte long.
let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
// Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyhash](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyhash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyrng](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyrng.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHash](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHash.html);

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# sandogasa-hattrack 0.15.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sandogasa-hattrack/0.15.3

# sandogasa-hattrack

Look up a Fedora contributor's activity across services.

## Installation

```
cargo install sandogasa-hattrack
```
## Usage

### Quick summary

```
$ sandogasa-hattrack last-seen salimma --no-fas
Last seen: salimma
  Dist-git       2026-03-20T23:59:59+00:00 (3 days ago)
                 last active on 2026-03-20
  Bodhi          2026-03-20T23:44:44+00:00 (3 days ago)
                 last update submitted
  Bugzilla       2026-03-20T15:14:06+00:00 (3 days ago)
                 #2449640 Tracker for invalid, cross-ecosystem CVE
  Discourse      2026-03-18T10:51:27+00:00 (5 days ago)
                 last post
                 status:  🏖️ on vacation
                 expires: 2026-04-01 00:00 UTC (in 1 week)
  Mailing lists  2026-03-13T09:58:20+00:00 (1 week ago)
                 Retiring python-sphinx-hoverxref
```
### Subcommands

- `bodhi`— recent Bodhi updates and comments
- `bugzilla`— recent Bugzilla activity
- `distgit`— dist-git activity, PRs filed, and PRs awaiting review
- `discourse`— Discourse profile and activity
- `last-seen`— summary of last activity across all services, including Discourse custom status and expiration
- `mailman`— mailing list posts via HyperKitty

### Email discovery

Subcommands that need an email address (bugzilla, mailman) will:

- Always try `username@fedoraproject.org`
- Query FASJSON for additional emails (requires Kerberos)
- Use `--email`for direct override,`--no-fas`to skip FASJSON

### Local time and weekend signal

The `discourse` subcommand resolves the user's IANA timezone to
a country (via the tzdb `zone1970.tab` table), then reports the
local time and whether it's currently the weekend in that
country. Weekends default to Sat+Sun, with overrides for places
where the workweek is shifted (Fri+Sat across most of MENA,
Fri only in Iran, Sat only in Nepal).

The lookup table is read from `/usr/share/zoneinfo/zone1970.tab`
by default; if that's older than the copy bundled with this
tool, an `info:` line on stderr notes that the bundled copy is
being used instead. Force one or the other with `--tz-source system` / `--tz-source bundled`.

The weekday tag is coloured (green for weekday, yellow for
weekend) and the time itself is dimmed when the local hour
falls outside working hours. Defaults to `9-18`; override with
`--working-hours <START-END>`. Colours follow the grep/ls
convention: `--color auto` (default) enables them on a TTY
when `NO_COLOR` is unset; `--color always` / `--color never`
force a choice.

The same `Local time:` / `Country:` block also appears at the
top of `last-seen` output. Both FAS (via FASJSON) and
Discourse are queried independently: matching timezones
collapse to one entry, mismatched ones are shown side-by-side
with a `[FAS]` / `[Discourse]` suffix so you can spot a
traveller who's updated one source but not the other.

### Public-holiday flag

When the user's resolved country has a nationwide public
holiday on their local date, a `Holiday:` line appears under
`Country:`. Data comes from the [Nager.Date](https://date.nager.at)
public API (122 countries) and is cached per country-per-year
under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/sandogasa-hattrack/holidays/`, so
repeat lookups never touch the network.

- `--no-holidays`skips the lookup entirely.
- `--refresh-holidays`force-refetches the cached data.
- `--now <YYYY-MM-DD>`overrides the date for testing, e.g.- `--now 2026-03-17 discourse salimma`to see what St. Patrick's Day looks like.

### Narrowing the `last-seen` service set

`last-seen` queries five services (Bodhi, Bugzilla, Discourse,
dist-git, Mailman). The Mailman scan is the slow path because
it walks HyperKitty archives page by page, so skipping it is
the common speed-up when the user clearly doesn't post:

```
```
`--skip` and `--only` are mutually exclusive. Both accept a
comma-separated list (or can be repeated). Values:
`bodhi`, `bugzilla`, `discourse`, `distgit`, `mailman`.

### JSON output

All subcommands support `--json` for machine-readable output:

```
$ sandogasa-hattrack --json last-seen salimma --no-fas
```

at your option.

# cu29_unifiedlog - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cu29-unifiedlog/1.0.0/cu29_unifiedlog/

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use noop::`- [NoopLogger](https://docs.rs/noop/struct.NoopLogger.html);
- `pub use noop::`- [NoopSectionStorage](https://docs.rs/noop/struct.NoopSectionStorage.html);
- `pub use crate::memmap::`- [LogPosition](https://docs.rs/memmap/struct.LogPosition.html);
- `pub use crate::memmap::`- [MmapUnifiedLogger](https://docs.rs/memmap/enum.MmapUnifiedLogger.html)as UnifiedLogger;
- `pub use crate::memmap::`- [MmapUnifiedLoggerBuilder](https://docs.rs/memmap/struct.MmapUnifiedLoggerBuilder.html)as UnifiedLoggerBuilder;

- `pub use crate::memmap::`- [MmapUnifiedLoggerWrite](https://docs.rs/memmap/struct.MmapUnifiedLoggerWrite.html)as UnifiedLoggerWrite;
- `pub use crate::memmap::`- [UnifiedLoggerIOReader](https://docs.rs/memmap/struct.UnifiedLoggerIOReader.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [memmap](https://docs.rs/memmap/index.html)
- This is the memory map file implementation for the unified logger for Copper. It is std only.
- [noop](https://docs.rs/noop/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [EndOf](https://docs.rs/struct.EndOfLogMarker.html)- LogMarker
- Payload stored in the end-of-log section to signal whether the log was cleanly closed.
- [LogStream](https://docs.rs/struct.LogStream.html)
- A wrapper around the unifiedlogger that implements the Write trait.
- [Main](https://docs.rs/struct.MainHeader.html)- Header
- The main file header of the datalogger.
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionHandle.html)- Handle
- A SectionHandle is a handle to a section in the datalogger. It allows tracking the lifecycle of the section.
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionHeader.html)- Header
- Each concurrent sublogger is tracked through a section header. They form a linked list of sections. The entry type is used to identify the type of data in the section.
- [Unified](https://docs.rs/struct.UnifiedLogStatus.html)- LogStatus
- Basic statistics for the unified logger. Note: the total_allocated_space might grow for the std implementation

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [MAIN_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAIN_MAGIC.html)- MAGIC
- ID to spot the beginning of a Copper Log
- [SECTION_](https://docs.rs/constant.SECTION_HEADER_COMPACT_SIZE.html)- HEADER_ - COMPACT_ - SIZE
- [SECTION_](https://docs.rs/constant.SECTION_MAGIC.html)- MAGIC
- ID to spot a section of Copper Log
- [UNIFIED_](https://docs.rs/constant.UNIFIED_LOG_FORMAT_VERSION.html)- LOG_ - FORMAT_ - VERSION
- Version of the unified log file format.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Section](https://docs.rs/trait.SectionStorage.html)- Storage
- A Storage is an append-only structure that can update a header section.
- [Unified](https://docs.rs/trait.UnifiedLogRead.html)- LogRead
- Read back a unified log linearly.
- [Unified](https://docs.rs/trait.UnifiedLogWrite.html)- LogWrite
- The writing interface to the unified logger. Writing is “almost” linear as various streams can allocate sections and track them until they drop them.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [stream_](https://docs.rs/fn.stream_write.html)- write
- Create a new stream to write to the unifiedlogger.

# hs-meetings 0.15.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hs-meetings/0.15.3

# hs-meetings

List and sync CentOS Hyperscale SIG meeting archives from
[meetbot.fedoraproject.org](https://meetbot.fedoraproject.org).

The SIG holds biweekly meetings on Matrix; zodbot logs them as
`centos-hyperscale-sig` topic sessions. This tool wraps meetbot's
search endpoint so the archive list in the SIG docs can be
maintained from the command line rather than by hand.

## Installation

```
```
## Subcommands

`list`

Fetches every meeting whose topic contains the search string (default
`centos-hyperscale-sig`), sorted ascending by date. `--period`
accepts `YYYY`, `YYYYQ1..Q4`, `YYYYH1..H2`; `--since` / `--until`
take `YYYY-MM-DD`. Output is a two-line-per-meeting table (date +
stacked summary/logs URLs) or a JSON array with `--json`.

`sync`

Fetches meetings from meetbot, deduplicates against entries
already present in `--file` (matching by date extracted from
the URL), and inserts any new ones into the correct `### YYYY`
section in reverse-chronological order. New year sections are
created as needed, newest-first. Year headings are rendered at
`###` level so they nest under the docs site's `## Meeting minutes` parent heading.

Meetings from 2023 and earlier are dropped before insertion:
pre-2024 sections predate meetbot and often carry hand-curated
`[agenda](...)` links, so the tool leaves them untouched. The
recommended docs layout is therefore to keep only the 2024+
sections in the tool-managed file and leave the legacy years
inline in `meetings.md`, which the docs site pulls together via
`pymdownx.snippets`:

```
# mkdocs.yml
markdown_extensions:
  - pymdownx.snippets
```
```
--8<-- "communication/meetings-list.md"
*
...
```
`hs-meetings sync` then owns `meetings-list.md` and can rewrite
it freely. New entries are rendered without an `agenda,` prefix
since no SIG meeting has had an external agenda link since
January 2023.

## License

Licensed under either of

at your option.

# wyhash 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/0.6.0

# wyhash fast portable non-cryptographic hashing algorithm

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark (faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need hardware support, can be
used in `no_std` environments) and has no dependencies (except the traits from `rand_core`).

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated [here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt)
although the speed varies ([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

## Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different results.

## Usage

This crate provides free functions as well as implementations of the `Hasher`, `BuildHasher`, `Rng` and
`SeedableRng` traits.

```
use Hasher;
use WyHash;
```
See further examples of the hasher and RNG in the documentation.

## Performance comparison

A basic performance comparison benchmark against [ fnv](https://crates.io/crates/fnv),

[,](https://crates.io/crates/twox-hash)

`twox-hash`[and the standard hash_map hash](https://crates.io/crates/metrohash)

`metrohash`[is included in the sources and you can run it with nightly Rust:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/hash_map/struct.DefaultHasher.html)

`collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher````
cargo +nightly bench
```
## Support

For questions, issues, feature requests, and other changes, please file an
[issue in the github project](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues).

## Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.63.0 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

## License

Licensed under either of

- Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)or[http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0](http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0))
- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)or[http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT))

at your option.

### Contributing

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

                    wyhash 0.6.0

# wyhash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/0.6.0/target-redirect/wyhash/

## Expand description

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
(faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
no dependencies.

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt) although the speed varies
([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different the results.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-see-also-examples-folder)Usage (see also examples folder)

For the hashing function you can use either the free function or the
`Hasher` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#wyhash-function-usage)`wyhash` function usage

```
use wyhash::wyhash;
let data = [0, 1, 2];
let seed = 3;
let hash = wyhash(&data, seed);
println!("{:x}", hash); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hasher-trait-usage)`Hasher` trait usage

You can also use `std::hash::Hasher`, it is the same.

```
use core::hash::Hasher;
use wyhash::WyHash;
let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
println!("{:x}", hasher.finish()); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#wyrng-function-usage)`wyrng` function usage

Note that the seed parameter is updated so that it is possible to generate a sequence of random numbers.

```
use wyhash::wyrng;
let mut seed = 3;
let random_number = wyrng(&mut seed);
println!("{:x}", random_number); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
println!("{:x}", seed); //prints a0761d6478bd6432
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rngcore-trait-usage)`RngCore` trait usage

You can also use `rand::Rng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::RngCore;
use wyhash::WyRng;
let mut rng = WyRng::default();
println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
```
[§](https://docs.rs#seedablerng-trait-usage)`SeedableRng` trait usage

You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};
use wyhash::WyRng;
// Seeds are 8-byte long.
let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
// Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyhash](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyhash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyrng](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyrng.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHash](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHasherBuilder](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHasherBuilder.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyRng](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyRng.html);

---

# wyhash

                    There is very little structured metadata to build this page

This feature flag does not enable additional features.

# wyhash - Rust

println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
```
[§](https://docs.rs#seedablerng-trait-usage)`SeedableRng` trait usage

You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};
use wyhash::WyRng;
// Seeds are 8-byte long.
let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
// Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
```

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/wyhash/0.6.0/src/wyhash/lib.rs.html

# wyhash/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi][original].
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! passes BigCrush and practrand.
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! (faster than t1ha and XXH3).
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! See [here][original].
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! no dependencies.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! [here][original-version] although the speed varies
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! ([PRs are welcome][issue-tracker]).
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! [issue-tracker]: https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! [original]: https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! [original-version]: https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! ## Crate features
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! performance on 32-bit architectures.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! Beware that this feature produces different the results.
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! ## Usage (see also examples folder)
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! For the hashing function you can use either the free function or the
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! `Hasher` trait.
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! ### `wyhash` function usage
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ```
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! use wyhash::wyhash;
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! let data = [0, 1, 2];
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! let seed = 3;
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! let hash = wyhash(&data, seed);
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! println!("{:x}", hash); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! ```
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! ### `Hasher` trait usage
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! You can also use `std::hash::Hasher`, it is the same.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! ```
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! use core::hash::Hasher;
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! use wyhash::WyHash;
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! println!("{:x}", hasher.finish()); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! ```
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! ### `wyrng` function usage
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! Note that the seed parameter is updated so that it is possible to
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! generate a sequence of random numbers.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! ```
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! use wyhash::wyrng;
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! let mut seed = 3;
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! let random_number = wyrng(&mut seed);
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! println!("{:x}", random_number); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! println!("{:x}", seed); //prints a0761d6478bd6432
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! ```
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! ### `RngCore` trait usage
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! You can also use `rand::Rng`, it is the same.
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! ```
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! use rand_core::RngCore;
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! use wyhash::WyRng;
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! let mut rng = WyRng::default();
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! ```
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! ### `SeedableRng` trait usage
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! ```
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! use wyhash::WyRng;
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! // Seeds are 8-byte long.
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! // Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! ```
[103](https://docs.rs#103)
[104](https://docs.rs#104)#![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/wyhash/0.5.0")]
[105](https://docs.rs#105)#![no_std]
[106](https://docs.rs#106)#![deny(missing_docs, unsafe_code)]
[107](https://docs.rs#107)
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// WyHash version 1
[109](https://docs.rs#109)pub mod v1;
[110](https://docs.rs#110)pub use crate::v1::{wyhash, wyrng};
[111](https://docs.rs#111)pub use crate::v1::{WyHash, WyHasherBuilder, WyRng};
[112](https://docs.rs#112)
[113](https://docs.rs#113)/// WyHash version final 3
[114](https://docs.rs#114)pub mod final3;

#### fn [try_next_u64](https://docs.rs/rand_core/0.9.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rand_core/trait.TryRngCore.html#tymethod.try_next_u64)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u64.html), <R as [TryRngCore](https://docs.rs/rand_core/0.9.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rand_core/trait.TryRngCore.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/rand_core/0.9.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rand_core/trait.TryRngCore.html#associatedtype.Error)>

`u64`.

# wyhash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wyhash/latest/wyhash/

## Expand description

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
(faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
no dependencies.

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt) although the speed varies
([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different the results.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-see-also-examples-folder)Usage (see also examples folder)

For the hashing function you can use either the free function or the
`Hasher` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#wyhash-function-usage)`wyhash` function usage

```
use wyhash::wyhash;
let data = [0, 1, 2];
let seed = 3;
let hash = wyhash(&data, seed);
println!("{:x}", hash); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hasher-trait-usage)`Hasher` trait usage

You can also use `std::hash::Hasher`, it is the same.

```
use core::hash::Hasher;
use wyhash::WyHash;
let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
println!("{:x}", hasher.finish()); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#wyrng-function-usage)`wyrng` function usage

Note that the seed parameter is updated so that it is possible to generate a sequence of random numbers.

```
use wyhash::wyrng;
let mut seed = 3;
let random_number = wyrng(&mut seed);
println!("{:x}", random_number); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
println!("{:x}", seed); //prints a0761d6478bd6432
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rngcore-trait-usage)`RngCore` trait usage

You can also use `rand::Rng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::RngCore;
use wyhash::WyRng;
let mut rng = WyRng::default();
println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
```
[§](https://docs.rs#seedablerng-trait-usage)`SeedableRng` trait usage

You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};
use wyhash::WyRng;
// Seeds are 8-byte long.
let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
// Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyhash](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyhash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyrng](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyrng.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHash](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHasherBuilder](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHasherBuilder.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyRng](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyRng.html);

# rand_core 0.9.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rand_core/^0.9

# rand_core

Core traits and error types of the [rand](https://crates.io/crates/rand) library, plus tools for implementing
RNGs.

This crate is intended for use when implementing the core trait, `RngCore`; it
defines the core traits to be implemented as well as several small functions to
aid in their implementation and types required for error handling.

The main [rand](https://crates.io/crates/rand) crate re-exports most items defined in this crate, along with
tools to convert the integer samples generated by `RngCore` to many different
applications (including sampling from restricted ranges, conversion to floating
point, list permutations and secure initialisation of RNGs). Most users should
prefer to use the main [rand](https://crates.io/crates/rand) crate.

Links:

## Functionality

The `rand_core` crate provides:

- base random number generator traits
- error-reporting types
- functionality to aid implementation of RNGs

The traits and error types are also available via `rand`.

## Versions

The current version is:

```
 = "0.9.0"
```

[COPYRIGHT](https://docs.rs/COPYRIGHT) for details.

# fnv 1.0.7 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fnv/^1

# rust-fnv

An implementation of the [Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function](http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html).

## About

The FNV hash function is a custom `Hasher` implementation that is more
efficient for smaller hash keys.

[The Rust FAQ states that](https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US/faq.html#why-are-rusts-hashmaps-slow) while the default `Hasher` implementation,
SipHash, is good in many cases, it is notably slower than other algorithms
with short keys, such as when you have a map of integers to other values.
In cases like these, [FNV is demonstrably faster](https://cglab.ca/~abeinges/blah/hash-rs/).

Its disadvantages are that it performs badly on larger inputs, and provides no protection against collision attacks, where a malicious user can craft specific keys designed to slow a hasher down. Thus, it is important to profile your program to ensure that you are using small hash keys, and be certain that your program could not be exposed to malicious inputs (including being a networked server).

The Rust compiler itself uses FNV, as it is not worried about denial-of-service attacks, and can assume that its inputs are going to be small—a perfect use case for FNV.

## Usage

To include this crate in your program, add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "1.0.3"
```
## Using FNV in a HashMap

The `FnvHashMap` type alias is the easiest way to use the standard library’s
`HashMap` with FNV.

```
use FnvHashMap;
let mut map = default;
map.insert;
map.insert;
map = with_capacity_and_hasher;
map.insert;
map.insert;
```
Note, the standard library’s `HashMap::new` and `HashMap::with_capacity`
are only implemented for the `RandomState` hasher, so using `Default` to
get the hasher is the next best option.

## Using FNV in a HashSet

Similarly, `FnvHashSet` is a type alias for the standard library’s `HashSet`
with FNV.

```
use FnvHashSet;
let mut set = default;
set.insert;
set.insert;
set = with_capacity_and_hasher;
set.insert;
set.insert;
```

# metrohash 1.0.7 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/metrohash/^1

# Rust MetroHash

MetroHash is a high quality, high performance hash algorithm.

It hashes small keys in the single digit nanoseconds and surpasses 10+ GB/s in medium to long length keys.

Since the hash quality is also excellent (passes SMhasher), it's a good alternative in any situation where cryptographic security is not required.

Note that the algorithm is not stable across different endianesses and is optimized for 64bit platforms with fast unaligned memory access.

# Usage

```
extern crate metrohash;
use MetroHashMap;
let mut hash = default;
hash.insert;
assert_eq!;
```

# twox-hash 2.1.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/twox-hash/^2.1

A Rust implementation of the [xxHash](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash) algorithm.

# Examples

These examples use [ XxHash64](crate::XxHash64) but the same ideas can be
used for

[,](crate::XxHash32)

`XxHash32`[, or](crate::XxHash3_64)

`XxHash3_64`[.](crate::XxHash3_128)

`XxHash3_128`## Hashing arbitrary data

### When all the data is available at once

```
use XxHash64;
let seed = 1234;
let hash = oneshot;
assert_eq!;
```
### When the data is streaming

```
use Hasher as _;
use XxHash64;
let seed = 1234;
let mut hasher = with_seed;
hasher.write;
hasher.write;
hasher.write;
let hash = hasher.finish;
assert_eq!;
```
## In a `HashMap`

`HashMap`### With a default seed

```
use ;
use XxHash64;
let mut hash = default;
hash.insert;
assert_eq!;
```
### With a random seed

```
use HashMap;
use xxhash64;
let mut hash = default;
hash.insert;
assert_eq!;
```
### With a fixed seed

```
use HashMap;
use xxhash64;
let mut hash = with_hasher;
hash.insert;
assert_eq!;
```
# Feature Flags

| name | description |
|---|---|
| xxhash32 | Include the algorithm`XxHash32` |
| xxhash64 | Include the algorithm`XxHash64` |
| xxhash3_64 | Include the algorithm`XxHash3_64` |
| xxhash3_128 | Include the algorithm`XxHash3_128` |
| random | Create random instances of the hashers |
| serialize | Serialize and deserialize hasher state with Serde |
| std | Use the Rust standard library. Enable this if you want SIMD support in or`XxHash3_64``XxHash3_128` |
| alloc | Use the Rust allocator library. Enable this if you want to create or`XxHash3_64`with dynamic secrets`XxHash3_128` |

# Benchmarks

See benchmarks in the [comparison](https://github.com/shepmaster/twox-hash/tree/main/comparison) README.

# wyhash 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/0.5.0

# wyhash fast portable non-cryptographic hashing algorithm

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark (faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need hardware support, can be
used in `no_std` environments) and has no dependencies (except the traits from `rand_core`).

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated [here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/original/CMakeLists.txt)
although the speed varies ([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

### Usage

```
use WyHash;
use Hasher;
```
See further examples of the hasher and RNG in the documentation.

## Support

For questions, issues, feature requests, and other changes, please file an
[issue in the github project](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues).

## Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)

This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.36.0 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.

# wyhash 0.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/0.3.0

# wyhash fast portable non-cryptographic hashing algorithm

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark (faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need hardware support, can be
used in `no_std` environments) and has no dependencies (except the traits from `rand_core`).

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated [here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/original/CMakeLists.txt)
although the speed varies ([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

### Usage

```
extern crate wyhash;
use WyHash;
use Hasher;
```
See further examples of the hasher and RNG in the documentation.

## Support

For questions, issues, feature requests, and other changes, please file an
[issue in the github project](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues).

## License

- Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)or[http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0](http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0))
- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)or[http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT))

at your option.

# wyhash 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/0.1.0

# Rust implementation of the wyhash fast non-cryptographic hashing algorithm

This is a Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).
The generated hashes are equal (see tests).

### Usage

`no_std` mode is activated by setting `default-features = false;`

```
extern crate wyhash;
use WyHash;
use Hasher;
```
## Status

- Hashing function
- PRNG

## Support

For questions, issues, feature requests, and other changes, please file an
[issue in the github project](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues).

# wyhash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wyhash

## Expand description

Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator
passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark
(faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash).

Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need
hardware support, can be used in `no_std` environments) and has
no dependencies.

The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated
[here](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/blob/master/comparison/original/CMakeLists.txt) although the speed varies
([PRs are welcome](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/issues)).

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate features

By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different the results.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-see-also-examples-folder)Usage (see also examples folder)

For the hashing function you can use either the free function or the
`Hasher` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#wyhash-function-usage)`wyhash` function usage

```
use wyhash::wyhash;
let data = [0, 1, 2];
let seed = 3;
let hash = wyhash(&data, seed);
println!("{:x}", hash); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hasher-trait-usage)`Hasher` trait usage

You can also use `std::hash::Hasher`, it is the same.

```
use core::hash::Hasher;
use wyhash::WyHash;
let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
println!("{:x}", hasher.finish()); // prints b0f941520b1ad95d
```
[§](https://docs.rs#wyrng-function-usage)`wyrng` function usage

Note that the seed parameter is updated so that it is possible to generate a sequence of random numbers.

```
use wyhash::wyrng;
let mut seed = 3;
let random_number = wyrng(&mut seed);
println!("{:x}", random_number); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
println!("{:x}", seed); //prints a0761d6478bd6432
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rngcore-trait-usage)`RngCore` trait usage

You can also use `rand::Rng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::RngCore;
use wyhash::WyRng;
let mut rng = WyRng::default();
println!("{:x}", rng.next_u64()); // prints 111cb3a78f59a58e
```
[§](https://docs.rs#seedablerng-trait-usage)`SeedableRng` trait usage

You can also use `rand::SeedableRng`, it is the same.

```
use rand_core::{RngCore, SeedableRng};
use wyhash::WyRng;
// Seeds are 8-byte long.
let seed = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
let mut rng1 = WyRng::from_seed(seed);
println!("{:x}", rng1.next_u64()); // prints d730135774c6ae31
// Alternatively you can also use this convenience method:
let mut rng2 = WyRng::seed_from_u64(3);
println!("{:x}", rng2.next_u64()); // prints 3e99a772750dcbe
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyhash](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyhash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [wyrng](https://docs.rs/v1/fn.wyrng.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHash](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHash.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyHasherBuilder](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyHasherBuilder.html);
- `pub use crate::v1::`- [WyRng](https://docs.rs/v1/struct.WyRng.html);

# wyhash 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wyhash/latest/source/README.md

```
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/wyhash.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/wyhash)
[![Docs](https://docs.rs/wyhash/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/wyhash)
![MSRV](https://img.shields.io/badge/rustc-1.63+-blue.svg)
[![Build Status](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/workflows/Build/badge.svg)](https://github.com/eldruin/wyhash-rs/actions?query=workflow%3ABuild)
[![Coverage Status](https://coveralls.io/repos/github/eldruin/wyhash-rs/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://coveralls.io/github/eldruin/wyhash-rs?branch=master)
Rust implementation of the [wyhash algorithm by Wang Yi][original].
The hashing algorithm passes SMHasher and the random number generator passes BigCrush and practrand.
As of now it is the fastest algorithm in the SMHasher benchmark (faster than t1ha and XXH3).
See [here][original].
Furthermore, this algorithm is solid, simple, portable (does not need hardware support, can be
used in `no_std` environments) and has no dependencies (except the traits from `rand_core`).
The generated hashes are equal (see tests) as of the version stated [here][original-version]
although the speed varies ([PRs are welcome][issue-tracker]).
By default this crate uses 128-bit integer multiplications.
To restrict that to 64 bits you can enable the feature `mum32bit`. This offers better
performance on 32-bit architectures.
Beware that this feature produces different results.
This crate provides free functions as well as implementations of the `Hasher`, `BuildHasher`, `Rng` and
`SeedableRng` traits.
```rust
use core::hash::Hasher;
use wyhash::WyHash;
fn main() {
  let mut hasher = WyHash::with_seed(3);
  hasher.write(&[0, 1, 2]);
  assert_eq!(0xcc24_2106_e707_6a48, hasher.finish());
}
```
See further examples of the hasher and RNG in the documentation.
A basic performance comparison benchmark against [`fnv`], [`twox-hash`], [`metrohash`]
and the standard hash_map hash [`collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher`][hash-map-hash]
is included in the sources and you can run it with nightly Rust:
```
cargo +nightly bench
```
For questions, issues, feature requests, and other changes, please file an
[issue in the github project][issue-tracker].
This crate is guaranteed to compile on stable Rust 1.63.0 and up. It *might*
compile with older versions but that may change in any new patch release.
Licensed under either of
 *  *
at your option.
Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted
for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall
be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.
```

# rand_core 0.9.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rand_core/0.9.5

# rand_core

Core traits and error types of the [rand](https://crates.io/crates/rand) library, plus tools for implementing
RNGs.

This crate is intended for use when implementing the core trait, `RngCore`; it
defines the core traits to be implemented as well as several small functions to
aid in their implementation and types required for error handling.

The main [rand](https://crates.io/crates/rand) crate re-exports most items defined in this crate, along with
tools to convert the integer samples generated by `RngCore` to many different
applications (including sampling from restricted ranges, conversion to floating
point, list permutations and secure initialisation of RNGs). Most users should
prefer to use the main [rand](https://crates.io/crates/rand) crate.

Links:

## Functionality

The `rand_core` crate provides:

- base random number generator traits
- error-reporting types
- functionality to aid implementation of RNGs

The traits and error types are also available via `rand`.

## Versions

The current version is:

```
 = "0.9.0"
```

[COPYRIGHT](https://docs.rs/COPYRIGHT) for details.
